text:
maya: Quick dump from a small bring-up today. Goal: validate dynamic-pooling + pruning for speculative decode on a quantized 13B (titan-13b-q4). Sharing raw notes.
maya: Setup: dynamic candidate pool (start 6, prune to 2 by token 40 based on JS-divergence), fastpath running int8 slices, rescoring via a cheap cross-encoder fp16 (score candidates without full autoreg decode). fallback policy: if composite trigger (entropy>2.9 OR mean_JS>0.18 OR length_ratio<0.75) then full fp16 fallback.
trent: neat. why JS-divergence instead of pairwise KL?
maya: JS is symmetric and bounded; easier to calibrate across token lengths. also cheaper numerically when we average distributions across top-k.
ivy: top-line latency and quality?
maya: median token latency ~2.9x better vs fp16 baseline for interactive prompts. end-to-end response time using pruning+rescoring ~2.4x. p95 down ~1.7x.
louis: metrics? any impact on benchmarks?
maya: automated: MMLU drop -0.5% (paired), TruthfulQA micro drop ~-0.6%, SQuAD EM -0.7%. sign-test p-values around 0.08 for most, so marginal. human spot-check (120 pairs) found 7 cases of premature truncation and 5 named-entity hallucinations where all top candidates agreed. rescoring fixed 4 of the 5 hallucinations.
trent: interesting that pruning helps latency but might reduce diversity. did you try stochastic top-k sampling within pool?
maya: yes briefly. stochastic diversity (top-k sampling) reduced some collusion but increased variance in answers; we need to quantify tradeoff. maybe hybrid: deterministic greedy for tokens with low uncertainty, stochastic otherwise.
ivy: can you paste the eval command?
maya: ```
redwood-evals run --suite bringup-dynpool:v1 \
  --model titan-13b-q4-dynspec \
  --rescoring-model fp16-titan-13b-xenc \
  --spec-start-pool 6 --spec-min-pool 2 --prune-by js_divergence \
  --js-threshold 0.18 --entropy-thresh 2.9 \
  --samples 2500 --tag dynprune-smoke-01
```
ci-bot: Job jd-6100 created, artifacts at /artifacts/spec/3012345678/ (logs, candidate distributions, rescoring outputs).
louis: ops concerns? memory/throughput tradeoffs?
maya: pruning reduces memory pressure because we retire KV states for pruned candidates early. rescoring cost small (forward-only per-candidate) and can be batched. net GPU cycles down ~42% by our rough accounting; rescoring adds back ~6% so net ~36% improvement.
trent: propose we log two new diagnostics for canary: per-token mean_JS, pool_size_over_time, and rescoring_delta (rescored_score - fastpath_score). Use these to tune thresholds.
maya: good call. Also propose a cheap early-exit: if top candidate probability >0.92 and mean_JS<0.03 then accept immediately (saves rescoring).
ivy: safety gating? what blocks rollout?
maya: recommend blocking if MMLU drops >1.0% with p<0.01 OR rare-entity QA hallucation rate increases by >0.3% on a 10k holdout. Also require human eval 1k paired samples for chain-of-thought prompts.
louis: I'll create canary ticket and reserve a 4% dedicated slice for 48 hours. ops-bot: created RED-2301: "dynpool spec decode canary titan-13b" https://jira.redwood/browse/RED-2301
ci-bot: Artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/spec/3012345678/ (candidate logits, per-token JS traces, rescoring logs).
trent: I'll take the JS calibration and prototype stochastic-hybrid. ivy: I'll wire up human-eval instructions and the paired-sample labeling schema. maya: I'll run the 10k multilingual holdout overnight and upload results. tagging @trent @ivy @louis for review. :thumbsup:
